decisions.decision: V2-030 closes M7 in the local closure only: one process, one test binary, injected clocks, and the pure internal/scheduler planning boundary plus its in-memory apply boundary. It must not start a second OS process, a container, or a namespace, and it must not claim the M7 gate. The revised M7 completion condition -- two or more independent Runner execution entities (separate machines, or two containers on one host with injected clock skew) across two or more Repositories -- is V2-031's, and V2-031 may satisfy the 'two containers' half with the rootless user+mount namespace confinement V2-046 already measured in internal/runner/confinement.go instead of adding podman.
decisions.rationale: The two tasks were split because the properties they prove have different failure modes. Ordering, conflict, dependency, starvation and rollback are properties of one deterministic decision function over a bounded snapshot; they are provable exactly and cheaply in-process, and proving them under two real execution entities would only add nondeterminism without adding information. Duplicate ownership and clock disagreement across independent entities are the opposite: they are only observable when two entities genuinely disagree. Keeping the boundary explicit stops V2-030 from being read as gate evidence for a condition it structurally cannot witness, which is exactly the failure the M7 condition was revised to prevent.

decisions.decision: Connect internal/scheduler's scalar Priority to domain.PriorityAssessment's multi-factor evaluation by importing internal/domain read-only and giving Requirement an optional assessment. When no assessment is supplied, the resulting order must be byte-for-byte the order the current scalar path produces.
decisions.rationale: Sol ruled this connection inside V2-030's scope. domain.PriorityAssessment currently has zero references anywhere in the repository -- it is a declared but unused type, so the multi-factor allocation the product definition requires (value, urgency, risk, cost, dependency) is documented and modelled but nowhere computed. Making the scheduler the single consumer gives the type its first real use without inventing a second vocabulary. Requiring identical ordering in the no-assessment case is what lets all five existing tests keep passing under their own names, which turns backward compatibility into a measured fact instead of a hope.

decisions.decision: Record the comparison result as a Decision: Plan carries one decision record per candidate considered, holding the factor inputs, the computed score, the rank, whether it was assigned, and -- when it was not -- exactly one reason drawn from a closed, exhaustively enumerated set of reason constants.
decisions.rationale: Today Decide silently `continue`s past six distinct rejection paths (not ready, unmet dependency, isolated repository, already owned, resource conflict, no runner capacity), so a requirement that never runs is indistinguishable from one that was never considered. That is the observability gap the product definition's 'detect, stop, replan, integrate' clause depends on. A closed reason set enumerated by a table test also makes the rejection paths countable, which is what the starvation proof needs to attribute a wait to a cause.

decisions.decision: Prove the starvation-prevention condition as an asserted bound, not as an isolation property: under a flood of candidates and retries from one Repository, a waiting high-value requirement in a second Repository is assigned within a named maximum number of Decide/Apply ticks, and the same scenario provably fails to converge inside that bound when the aging/starvation term is removed.
decisions.rationale: The existing TestDecidePreventsDoubleOwnerAndIsolatesFailureStorm proves only that an isolated repository is excluded and a healthy one stays schedulable. That is failure-storm isolation, which is a different condition from 'one repository's mass demand, failures and retries do not keep occupying the capacity other important requirements need'. V2-019's own evidence assigns multi-Repository capacity starvation to V2-030, so it must be proven here. Without the negative control the bound could be satisfied by a scenario that never actually starves anything.

decisions.decision: Strengthen the cross-repository rollback assertion from all-or-nothing to convergence: the conflicting-claim path must leave the snapshot comparing equal to its pre-Apply value, and the immediately following Decide/Apply cycle on that same snapshot must reach a complete assignment without duplicating any claim or assignment.
decisions.rationale: The M7 condition is that cross-repository rollback converges, not merely that it rolls back. Apply already returns the original snapshot on ErrAtomicPlan and on ErrConflict, but nothing asserts that the system makes progress afterwards; a rollback that always rolls back again is a livelock that today's test would call a pass.

decisions.decision: Prove the scheduler's purity mechanically rather than by review: a go/parser import scan over the package's own *.go files, in the style of internal/domain/source_guard_test.go, allowing only the standard library and internal/domain, and failing outright on an empty file set.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/scheduler-local.md asserts the package performs no Firestore, network, process or provider operation, and validation.md section 5's growth-rate items depend on the decision cost being a function of the bounded snapshot alone. A prose assertion cannot hold that; an AST scan can, and it is also what keeps d2's new internal/domain import from silently becoming a door to a store or a real clock.

decisions.decision: Bound the reconcile budget with a context deadline and log the measured duration as an observation: 100 candidates across at least two Repositories and at least two Runner records must complete Decide plus Apply inside a 30 second context.WithTimeout, with durations at 10, 50 and 100 candidates recorded but never asserted as thresholds.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 5 fixes one reconcile tick at 100 items within 30 seconds, and MaxCandidates is already 100, but nothing measures it. V2-019's a6-batch-cursor-bound established the house precedent for this shape -- deadline as the assertion, duration as an observation -- which keeps the budget enforced without turning a timing number into a flaky assertion.

decisions.decision: Add the missing coverage for ResourceRequest.Global, which is documented as the installation-wide scope but has no test at all today.
decisions.rationale: Resource claim conflict is one of M7's named outcomes, and the global scope is the half of it that crosses repositories -- exactly the half a multi-Repository milestone cannot leave untested. An untested documented flag is also the cheapest place for a silent conflict-detection hole to live.

risks: Adding an internal/domain import to internal/scheduler makes ci/components.json's dependency list for the scheduler component wrong (it currently declares no dependencies), so the scheduler evidence key stops covering domain's public contracts. No test enforces that the declared DAG matches real imports, so this will not fail closed; it must be recorded as a measured observation for V2-045, which owns making the DAG match real imports, and ci/components.json must not be edited here.

Giving Plan a new Decisions field changes a struct that is compared and composite-literalled in the existing tests. The existing composite literal Plan{Assignments: ...} is field-named, so it still compiles, but any new comparison of whole Plan values must not be introduced, or the decision records would turn a behavioural assertion into a formatting assertion.

A multi-factor score can silently reorder the existing tests' candidates. The identical-order requirement for the no-assessment case is the only thing preventing that, so it must be asserted, not assumed.

The starvation bound is the one number in this task that encodes a policy judgement. If it is chosen after the fact to match whatever the implementation does, the test proves nothing; it must be stated as a named constant with a written justification before the aging term is tuned.

Editing docs/operations/scheduler-local.md moves the docs component evidence key as well as the scheduler one. Only the scheduler record is issued here; the docs key movement is recorded as a staleness note, resolved by V2-045's component re-issue under gate rule G6.
